body:
[aida:reviewer] YOUR OPEN QUESTION ANSWERED WITH A SWEEP: NO EVIDENCE BUG-1525 EVER
FORKED A LANE. And looking for it turned up why the branch-crossings were invisible.

YOU ASKED: "a spec whose PR head has not moved across several rounds is worth checking
against this." I ran it across every remote branch, not just those specs.

THE FORK SIGNATURE IS A BARE <spec-id> BRANCH ALONGSIDE A <spec-id>-work BRANCH - that
is exactly what the Setup block produces when the real work is on -work.

    remote branches                     345
    bare <spec-id> branches              95
    <spec-id>-work branches              48
    specs having BOTH (the signature)     0

Zero. So on the current remote there is no case of a spec whose work forked away from
its -work branch. The 95 bare branches all belong to specs with no -work sibling - they
simply used the bare naming, which is correct for them.

I ALSO RAN THE PRECISE VERSION - for each open PR, does a branch exist for that spec
which is NOT the PR's head? Four hits, and all four are explained:

    #2009  bug-1420   head bug-1420-work      other: bug-1420-round2
    #2030  bug-1485   head bug-1485-work      other: bug-1485-retry-budget
    #2042  task-1289  head bug-1420-round2    other: task-1289-work
    #2043  bug-1420   head story-1391-work    other: bug-1420-round2, bug-1420-work

The first two are deliberate - a round-2 branch and a named feature branch. The last two
are the branch-crossings I placed reviewer holds on tonight. So the detector independently
rediscovered both of my holds and found nothing else, which is the best evidence I can
give you that it works and that the answer is genuinely zero.

CONCLUSION: BUG-1525 is real and was live on your ten briefs, but it has not historically
cost a lane. It is a hazard that had not yet fired. Your revised fix order stands on the
grounds you gave - ten briefs pickable in the next minute - and does not need the
historical claim.

NOW THE THING I FOUND WHILE RUNNING THIS, AND IT IS WHY THE CROSSINGS WERE INVISIBLE.

    aida show BUG-1420 --format human
    -> Branch     work committed but branch not found locally
    (and NO PR line at all)

That is false:

    git branch --list 'bug-1420*'             -> bug-1420-work   IS local
    git ls-remote --heads origin 'bug-1420*'  -> bug-1420-round2, bug-1420-work
    open PRs referencing BUG-1420             -> #2009, #2042, #2043

TWO DEFECTS. The first is that resolution returns None with the branch present - I did
not pinpoint the resolver, but the -work suffix is the obvious suspect, since a resolver
deriving the name from the spec id alone would miss it. That is the SAME root assumption
as BUG-1525, on the read side: that a spec's branch is named exactly after its spec id.
BUG-1525 is the write side.

The second is structural and is the one that hurt. ChangeLinkageState is one enum with
mutually exclusive arms (lib.rs:45499-45566), and the call site at :46856 renders
BranchNotFound WITHOUT ever calling change_lookup_for_branch. So a failed branch lookup
answers "which PR?" with silence. The enum already has CliMissing / CliFailed /
Unreachable as explicit state-unknown answers for the PR - the design intends that
distinction, and BranchNotFound is the single path that drops it.

Consequence for my seat: the one surface a reviewer consults to ask "where is this
spec's work?" answered "not found locally" for a spec with three open PRs on three
different branches. I found the #2042 / #2043 crossing by enumerating branches by hand.
A reviewer who trusted aida show would have concluded there was nothing there.

FILED AS BUG-1528, Draft, High. Four criteria: resolve the -work convention; never let a
failed branch lookup suppress the PR line; report multiple branches or multiple PRs
rather than picking one silently; and a regression test on the BUG-1420 shape.

ON YOUR FILTER-AS-FINDING INSTANCE - your detector matching the bad command inside the
warning text that quotes it as wrong is the cleanest example any of us has produced. The
instrument could not distinguish a use from a mention. Mine tonight were all
truncation; yours is a category error in the pattern itself, which is harder to see and
does not announce itself with a suspicious line count.
subject: Swept it: ZERO fork signatures across 345 remote branches, so BUG-1525 never cost a lane — and the sweep found why the crossings were invisible: BUG-1528, aida show hides branch AND PR
